Capable of knocking back enemies and applying bleed.|Inventory Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Warlock''' is a melee and ranged hybrid ground tower that could have been unlocked by triumphing [[Outpost 16]], [[Banlands]] and [[Blind Faith]] on the Hard difficulty of the [[Null & Void Event]]. It could most recently be obtained via a limited-time gamepass for {{Robux|849}}. The '''Warlock''' has two range rings, each allows it to attack in a specific mode, each with its own statistics. The bigger range ring is the ranged attack range. With it, the '''Warlock''' fires energy beams at enemies. This deals damage to a single enemy, while also knocking it back at later levels. There is a 3 second cooldown before an enemy can be knocked back again. The second red range ring is the melee range. In it, the '''Warlock''' will attack enemies with its sword. This will deal AOE damage, with the intended target receiving both the melee and ranged damage, while anything hit alongside it only receives the ranged damage. This also applies bleed to enemies. If there are enemies in both its ranged and melee ranges, it will prioritize attacking enemies in its melee range. At Level 4, it gains the ability to apply bleed to enemies. Each bleed applied will only deal damage to an enemy once before disappearing, with there also being a 1.8 second delay between each bleed damage. Additionally, it can only deal damage while bleed is not being applied. This bleed can stack up to 40 times, which will cause a bleed collapse, dealing increased damage to the enemy instantly. The damage dealt varies based on an enemy's max health and the '''Warlock's''' base bleed damage, EV (exponential value) and how many bleed stacks are removed at once. Because of this, when the enemy receives bleed damage from the enemy over time, it is calculated as:
\text{(Base Bleed Damage} \times (1^{0.9})) \times (\text{Enemy Max Health}^{\text{EV}})
While bleed is collapsing on an enemy, it is calculated as:
\text{(Base Bleed Damage} \times (40^{0.9})) \times (\text{Enemy Max Health}^{\text{EV}})
Damage from bleed is always rounded up, for both damage over time and from bleed collapse. Additionally, damage from bleed damage will not be displayed as the full damage dealt for the '''Warlock''' unless only one '''Warlock''' was applying bleed. Damage displayed will be based on the number of bleed stacks applied by the selected '''Warlock'''. This damage is not affected by [[Damage Buff]]s. The '''Warlock''' can be considered a mid to late-game tower as its fairly effective during the mid and late game due to its high DPS, and its bleed effect that can affect every enemy, including major bosses. However, this is not always reliable as the '''Warlock''' prioritizes melee range and, due to various immunities related to knockback, prevents it from occurring consistently. *The '''Warlock''' will prioritize attacking enemies in the melee range, regardless of its targeting. **For example, if set to ''Last Enemy'' and there are enemies in both its melee and ranged range, it will only target the last enemy in its melee range, ignoring all enemies in the ranged range. **This can be beneficial in certain situations, such as allowing it to ignore [[Aggro]] or target specific enemies that you want it to target. However, it can also lead to scenarios where a '''Warlock's''' target escapes its melee range while other enemies remain in range, leaving a potentially strong enemy with nothing to defeat it. ***Because of this, other towers should be taken to help with anything that gets past the '''Warlock's''' range as it will quite often be unable to actually deal with it itself *Towers that decrease firerate, such as [[Commander]] can help the '''Warlock''' build bleed stacks more quickly. *Stalling towers are a great match with the '''Warlock''', as they can keep enemies in its melee range for longer. **They can also stall enemies that get past its melee range, giving it more time to kill enemies in melee range so that it can deal with leaks. **Note that Warlock has the highest knockback force of any tower in game, so use it to your advantage *The '''Warlock''' can be useful on maps that contain loops, such as [[Crossroads]]. ==Trivia== *The '''Warlock''' is the only tower to use melee attacks that has the default size of tower placement footprint. *The '''Warlock''' is the first tower to change attack modes based on enemies in its range. *The names of most of the tower upgrades likely reference different features from the tabletop game ''Dungeons and Dragons'': **While not a direct reference, Level 1 may be related to the Acolyte background, a feature that grants the Magic Initiate (Cleric) origin feat to any ''Dungeons and Dragons'' character. **Level 3 references Pact of the Blade, a subfeature of a class feature from the original ''Dungeons and Dragons'' Warlock called Eldritch Invocations. The feature evolves around the use of a Pact Weapon, further reinforcing the reference to the large sword the tower is carrying. **Level 4 references the Eldritch Knight, a subclass of the original ''Dungeons and Dragons'' Fighter that grants spellcasting to the purely martial class. *The Level 5 upgrade name may be a reference to the [[w:c:darksoulsKnight Artorias|Artorias The Abysswalker]] from ''Dark Souls''. ==Update History== ''For previous cosmetic variations, see the [[/Gallery|gallery]] page.'' {{scroll|text = *'''31 October 2025''' -
